newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- At least 52 new business deals worth $505.58 million were forged between Filipino and Canadian businessmen at the conclusion yesterday of the three-day state visit of Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien here. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- President Ramos said yesterday he will push through with the national identification reference system despite criticisms. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Energy Regulatory Board will announce today that prices of oil products will increase by an average of 52 centavos per litre effective tomorrow. (TIMES)
- Private sector employees in Metro Manila are likely to receive a daily wage adjustment of up to 20 pesos starting next month. (BUSINESSWORLD/CHRONICLE)

- The Palace has approved an optional budgetary allocation of 2.5 billion pesos to cover the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund deficit under the Supplemental Appropriation for 1997. (BULLETIN/INQUIRER/TIMES/STAR)
- The agricultural sector posted a 3.90 percent growth in value terms last year from a 1.79 percent expansion registered in 1995, the Department of Agriculture said yesterday. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
